body.p: Claims 1-20 are pending in the present application. Claims 1, 11 and 20 were amended in this Response. No new matter was introduced as a result of the amendments. Support for the amendments may be found, for example, in 10032 of the present specification ("[i]n some examples, it may be advantageous to remove or to reduce the restraining torque the braking torque is reduced with a lower torque reduction gradient than the restraining drive torque. In this manner, it can be achieved that there is always sufficient braking torque to reliably prevent any unanticipated acceleration of the vehicle. Aside from that, a reliable standstill of the vehicle can be ensured."). Entry of the amendments and favorable reconsideration is earnestly requested.

The Office Action states on page 2 that "[t]he drawings are objected to because the Examiner may require and is requiring descriptive text labels. Specifically, the unlabeled rectangular box(es) shown in the drawings should be provided with descriptive text labels (see Fig. 2)." Applicant has amended FIG. 2 to include the descriptive text labels, as indicated. Withdrawal of the objection is earnestly requested.

Claims 1, 6, 11 and 20 were objected to for minor informalities. In light of the present amendments to claims 1, 6, 11 and 20, Applicant submits the objectionable matter has been overcome. Withdrawal of the objection is earnestly requested.

Claims 20 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. §101 as allegedly being directed to non-statutory subject matter. In light of the present amendments to claim 20, clarifying "[a] non-transitory computer-readable medium" Applicant submits the rejection is overcome. Withdrawal of the rejection is earnestly requested.

Claims 1-7, 11-17 and 20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. §10 as allegedly being unpatentable over Takeya (US Pat. Pub. No. 2022/0017056) in view of Das et al. (US Pat. Pub. No. 2017/0297575). In light of the present amendments, Applicant submits the rejection is overcome.
Specifically, neither Takeya nor Das teach or suggest the features of amended independent claim 1, highlighted below:
1. A method for restrained movement of a vehicle comprising
a drive unit for accelerating the vehicle, and a braking unit for
braking the vehicle, comprising:
generating a restraining drive torque via the drive unit; generating a braking torque, via the braking unit, to compensate for the restraining drive torque and thereby generating
a restraining torque in the vehicle; and
braking the vehicle by reducing the restraining drive torque; and
reducing the restraining torque by reducing the braking torque and the restraining drive torque, wherein the braking
torque is reduced with a smaller torque reduction gradient than the restraining drive torque during the braking of the

None of the cited references teach or suggest these features. Takeya discloses a method involving a drive unit (driving force control unit) and a braking unit (braking force control unit) for controlling the movement of a vehicle (110020, 0046). Takeya describes balancing the driving and braking forces to maintain constant speed (10046). However, Takeya does not teach or suggest braking by reducing the drive torque. Instead, it discusses controlling the driving force while keeping the braking force constant (10052-53). Additionally, Takeya does not teach or suggest braking by reducing the drive torque. Instead, it discusses controlling the driving force while keeping the braking force constant (10052-53).

Das does not solve the deficiencies of Takeya, as Das discloses braking a vehicle by reducing the drive torque, specifically reducing creep torque until the vehicle comes to a standstill (paragraph 10022). Neither Das nor Takeya teach or suggest "wherein the braking torque is reduced with a smaller torque reduction gradient than the restraining drive torque during the braking of the vehicle." This specific control over the reduction gradients is a distinguishing feature

that provides a novel and non-obvious improvement over the prior art. As now recited in the amended claims, the specific control of torque reduction gradients during braking (wherein the braking torque is reduced with a smaller torque reduction gradient than the restraining drive torque) provides an improved technical advantage, namely more refined and smooth braking (see 0027 of the present Specification), which is not suggested or taught by the combination of Takeya and Das.

For at least these reasons, Applicant submits the rejection to amended independent claim 1 under 35 U.S.C. §103 is overcome and should be withdrawn. As amended independent claims 11 and 20 recite similar features, they are allowable for the same reasons. The remining dependent claims are allowable by virtue of their dependence upon their respective base claims.

In light of the present amendment and arguments, Applicants respectfully submit that the patent application is in condition for allowance and request an early Notice of Allowance. The Commissioner is authorized to charge and credit Deposit Account No. 50-5240 for any additional fees associated with the submission of this Response. Please reference docket number VW-1126 (K 30162 US).
